# switch_rom_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Trim or untrim Nintendo Switch cartridge images (.xci).

## Synopsis

```
switch_rom_tool [options]
```

## Description

Finds every `.xci` file under the input path (or takes the one file given) and runs
XCI Trimmer on a temporary copy of it. `-t` removes the unused padding at the end of
the image and writes `<name>_trimmed.xci`; `-u` pads a trimmed image back to its full
cartridge size and writes `<name>_untrimmed.xci`. Both are written next to the source.

With `-d` the source `.xci` is deleted after XCI Trimmer succeeds and the new file
has been moved into place.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | An `.xci` file, or a directory searched recursively for them; must exist. |
| `-t, --trim` | Trim each image into `<name>_trimmed.xci`. |
| `-u, --untrim` | Pad each image to full size into `<name>_untrimmed.xci`. |
| `-d, --delete_originals` | Delete the source `.xci` after it is trimmed or untrimmed. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Trim every XCI in a folder

```bash
switch_rom_tool -i /path/to/switch -t
```

### Trim and delete the originals, previewing first

```bash
switch_rom_tool -i /path/to/switch -t -d -p -v
```

### Pad one trimmed image back to full size

```bash
switch_rom_tool -i "/path/to/Game (USA).xci" -u
```

## Notes

- Without `-t` or `-u` nothing is done. If both are given, `-t` wins.
- Output files are also `.xci`, so running the tool again on the same folder processes them too.
- Each image is copied to the temporary directory first, which needs room for the image and its output.
- XCI Trimmer and the JoyBox Python environment must be installed as JoyBox tools.
